audit_findings.title: Arcosa completion would invalidate the as-filed earnings and financing perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.5 billion enterprise value; approximately $8.75 billion of expected additional indebtedness
audit_findings.mechanism: Completion would change both the equity-level OE numerator through Arcosa earnings and financing costs and the bridge through cash used, new debt, transaction costs and other acquired claims.
audit_findings.evidence: Significant acquisition activity could adversely affect our leverage profile and, in turn, adversely impact operating and financial flexibility as well as financial position.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking perimeter change, not an error in the current as-filed valuation. The acquisition had not closed and no Arcosa earnings or financing balances were included. Its eventual value effect is mixed because acquired owner earnings could add value while financing costs and claims reduce it. The scale is plainly capable of changing the conclusion once completion occurs.
audit_findings.action: At closing, rerun the valuation using the final purchase price, cash contribution, debt and equity issued, transaction costs, acquired minority claims and filed post-acquisition earnings including the full incremental interest burden.

audit_findings.title: Currently exercisable redeemable NCI is missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $435 million, or approximately $0.65 per diluted share; this equals the bull case's $0.65 premium over the $94.17 market price
audit_findings.mechanism: The currently exercisable redemption claim belongs in the common-equity bridge because the associated NCI earnings and redemption-value adjustments are excluded from the common-share numerator.
audit_findings.evidence: The noncontrolling interest holder has the right to sell the noncontrolling interests to the Company, which are currently exercisable.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the June 2026 filing reports $435 million of redeemable NCI, while the supplied bridge contains no corresponding deduction. A $0.65-per-share adjustment would consume the entire reported bull-case premium to market, so it can change that scenario's conclusion even though bear and base remain below market.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 formulaic redemption value and whether any part is already captured elsewhere, then rerun all scenarios with the verified common-equity claim deducted from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Recurring disposal gains may be supporting the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $235 million pre-tax in 2025 and $237 million in 2024; the 2025 amount is 6.5% of the $3,610.4 million anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any disposal gain retained in OE raises the anchor and is then capitalized through forecast growth and terminal value despite arising from asset sales rather than continuing operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Gain on disposal of long-lived assets was $235 million in 2025, a decrease of $2 million compared with 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are filed and recurring across the last two years, but their inclusion in the supplied OE series is not demonstrated. If retained, an item equal to 6.5% of the anchor is reasonably capable of changing value materially; the after-tax OE and valuation effects cannot be established without the annual reconciliations.
audit_findings.action: Audit the 2023-2025 OE reconciliations line by line for gains on long-lived assets and businesses, remove any retained after-tax gains, preserve related disposal costs, taxes and lost earnings, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Construction-contract estimates could reverse a material part of reported earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.693 billion of 2025 over-time service revenue exposed to estimation; any earnings overstatement is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Optimistic estimates of total contract costs accelerate recognized profit into reported earnings and OE and may also distort growth if later cost revisions reverse that profit.
audit_findings.evidence: We identified revenue recognized over time on construction contracts in-process as a critical audit matter because of the judgments necessary for management to estimate total contract costs at completion used to recognize revenue.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large estimate-dependent revenue population and the auditor identified it as a critical audit matter, but it does not demonstrate an error or quantify possible margin reversal. The issue may affect value, but the current record cannot establish materiality of any misstatement.
audit_findings.action: Compare completed-contract outcomes with original cost estimates, inspect subsequent margin revisions and loss provisions, reconcile changes in contract assets and unbilled revenue to cash collections, and rerun OE if forecast bias or reversals are identified.

audit_findings.title: Quarry-restoration obligations may not be fully represented by annual expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $436 million carrying obligation, including $79 million current, and $44 million of 2025 accretion and depreciation; approximately $0.65 per share if the full claim is otherwise omitted
audit_findings.mechanism: Restoration costs must reduce OE through normalized reclamation cash expenditure or maintenance capital expenditure, or remain as an after-tax settlement claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the carrying amount of the Company’s AROs were $ 436 million and $ 385 million, of which, $ 79 million and $ 66 million are current, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is filed, but the record does not demonstrate whether reclamation cash costs are already captured in OE, so a valuation error remains unresolved. The $436 million claim is about $0.65 per share, enough to eliminate the bull case's premium to market if otherwise omitted, making the issue materially capable despite the uncertain incremental adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Trace ARO additions, accretion, depreciation and actual settlement payments through each OE calculation and maintenance-capex classification; deduct only the verified after-tax amount not already represented, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The Philippines VIE can create a consolidated-to-common claim mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 VIE revenue of $310 million, net loss of $64 million and assets of $1.195 billion; OE allocation mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Using parent-attributable income but 100% of consolidated VIE depreciation, capital expenditure or working-capital movements mixes CRH's 55% economic entitlement with cash-flow adjustments belonging partly to the 45% outside interest.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s operations in the Philippines are conducted through a Variable Interest Entity (VIE), wherein the Company holds 40 % of the equity share capital and a 55 % share of earnings and distributions.
audit_findings.explanation: The ownership and economic-sharing mismatch is filed, but the supplied record does not show the entity-level components used in OE. Full depreciation addbacks could overstate value, while full capital-expenditure or working-capital deductions could understate it. The direction and materiality of the net mismatch therefore cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct the Philippines VIE contribution to net income, depreciation, maintenance capital expenditure and working-capital changes for every OE year, allocate each component to CRH's 55% economic share, verify that outside-holder cash and claims are excluded from the bridge, and rerun if a mismatch exists.
